The two ships have the same speed, so the only difference in their motion is their mass.  
A ship’s momentum is \(p = mv\). With the heavier cargo, the ship’s mass \(m\) is larger, giving it a larger momentum at the same speed.  

When the brakes (or reverse thrust) apply the same force to both ships, the deceleration \(a = F/m\) is smaller for the heavier ship, so it loses speed more slowly. Consequently, it requires more time to reduce its momentum to zero.  

Thus, the heavier‑cargo ship takes longer to stop because it has **greater momentum**.

**Final answer: B**
